paper_metadata.title: Recurrence of First Afebrile Unprovoked Seizure and Parental Consanguinity: A Hospital-Based Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the setting, recruitment period, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, as a hospital-based retrospective study in a tertiary center, there is a risk of referral bias (more severe cases). The participation rate of eligible individuals is not explicitly stated, making it difficult to rule out selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Children aged from I month to 16 years old who attended the hospital between January 2013 to December 2017 were evaluated on the basis of medical records
items.reasoning: The age range and clinical setting (pediatric clinic at a tertiary hospital) are clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: A list of patients... was identified using the hospital database. The diagnosis... was confirmed by a consultant neurologist using the criteria and classification of the International League Against Epilepsy.
items.reasoning: While the database search and diagnostic confirmation are described, the study does not address the potential bias of using a tertiary referral center (King Abdullah University Hospital) which may attract more complex cases.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between January 1, 2013, and December 31, 2017
items.reasoning: The dates are explicitly provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: King Abdullah University Hospital, the main tertiary referral center in the North of Jordan.
items.reasoning: The specific institution and its regional role are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Children who had experienced previous neonatal seizures, febrile seizure, myoclonic seizures, absences, infantile spasms, epileptic encephalopathy, or diagnosed epilepsy were excluded.
items.reasoning: Detailed exclusion criteria are provided to ensure the sample consists of first unprovoked seizures.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: During the study period, a total of 349 cases with first unprovoked seizure were identified. Fifty-nine cases were excluded... leaving 290 cases.
items.reasoning: The text does not state how many eligible patients might have been missed or if any records were inaccessible, though the use of a database suggests high capture of those who attended.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1 outlines the demographics and clinical data of all included cases.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides comprehensive data on age, gender, consanguinity, seizure type, and comorbidities.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study utilized hospital records and supplemental phone calls to minimize missing data. The follow-up period was fixed at 12 months, and the analysis included nearly all identified eligible patients (284/290 for the primary outcome).

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of the 290 first unprovoked seizure cases, more than half (157/284; 55.3%) had a recurrent seizure during the first 12 months of follow-up.
items.reasoning: 284 out of 290 patients (98%) were accounted for in the recurrence analysis.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Phone calls with the parents were used to check for any missing information.
items.reasoning: The authors proactively contacted parents to fill gaps in the retrospective records.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text does not explicitly state why 6 patients were missing from the final recurrence denominator (290 vs 284).

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no description of the 6 patients who did not provide outcome data.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The number of lost participants is very small (2%), so impact is likely minimal, but no formal comparison was made.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the primary prognostic factor (consanguinity) is straightforward, other factors like seizure type relied on parental history, which is prone to recall bias. Additionally, EEG and neuroimaging were only performed in less than 50% of the sample, leading to significant missing data for those specific predictors.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The data were collected for each patient on a structured specific form that included... parental consanguinity
items.reasoning: Consanguinity is mentioned but not strictly defined (e.g., first-cousin vs second-cousin) within the methods, though the discussion references first-cousin marriages.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Based on the history from parents, more than quarter of the patients (84/ 285; 29.5%) had a seizure with focal features.
items.reasoning: Reliance on parental recall for seizure semiology (focal vs generalized) is a known source of misclassification bias.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Continuous data were presented as median and interquartile range
items.reasoning: Age was treated appropriately; most other PFs were categorical.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The data were collected for each patient on a structured specific form
items.reasoning: A standardized form was used for all medical record reviews.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Electroencephalography (EEG) was done around the time of the first unprovoked seizure in fewer than half of patients (48.3%; 140/290)
items.reasoning: While demographic data was complete, clinical PFs like EEG and Neuroimaging had >50% missing data.

items.label: Method used for missing data

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure recurrence) is clearly defined according to international standards (ILAE) and the follow-up period is appropriate for the study goals.

items.evidence_snippet: Recurrence was defined as an unprovoked seizure occurring more than 24 hours after the first seizure... reviewed for 12 months
items.reasoning: The definition and timeframe are explicit.

items.reasoning: Expert clinical diagnosis using ILAE criteria is the gold standard for this outcome.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The hospital records of these cases were reviewed for 12 months to determine the incidence of recurrence.
items.reasoning: All patients were followed via the same hospital database and parental phone calls.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study adjusted for age and gender in the multivariate model. However, it did not adjust for other critical confounders like EEG or neuroimaging results in the final model, likely due to the high amount of missing data for those variables.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are standard and appropriate for the study design. The authors reported both univariate and multivariate results transparently, including effect sizes (OR) and confidence intervals.
